target_customer: Men who want to buy the clothing worn by celebrities and style influencers (free app); revenue from retail affiliate and commerce sales plus brand data
problem: Shoppers see a look on a celebrity or TV character and cannot easily find or buy the exact items or a cheaper match. Looklive matched pictured items to purchasable products.
business_model: Free consumer app earning commerce commissions on items sold, plus later brand data on product placement in TV shows
product_category: Social commerce and celebrity fashion discovery app

founders.name: Paul Judge
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him Dr. Paul Judge and says he is a co-founder and executive at several tech companies. His Judge Ventures co-invested in the seed. Degree not stated in sources opened.

founders.name: Cedric Rogers
prior_employers: Apple (10 years, worked on the App Store)
founders.background_notes: Interviewed in the YC launch post.

founders.name: Greg Selkoe
previous_startups: Karmaloop (founder, men's e-commerce, reported over $100 million annual sales per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: YC launch post and TechCrunch give different Karmaloop sales figures, so none is relied on.

competitors.name: Craves
competitors.what: Fashion app for men and women using visual search to find items

technical_complexity.rationale: Crawling celebrity photos, then matching pictured clothing to specific SKUs with image analysis and editors, was real but standard computer vision plus manual curation work for a small team in 2016.

defensibility.rationale: A catalog of matched looks and a merged user base gave some data advantage, but the idea of shopping celebrity looks was easy to copy by Instagram, Pinterest and other shopping apps.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in sources opened. The YC launch post named Pinterest, Instagram and style blogs as where shoppers searched for looks then. No source states that an incumbent copied or bought Looklive.

market_need_then: The YC launch post (2016-08-18) argued that existing men's online shopping did not work and cited store closures such as Macy's closing 100 stores. TechCrunch (2016-08-19) reported about 1 million monthly users and over $120,000 monthly GMV at launch, as company claims.

branding.name_origin: The Looklive name came from a company that Curateurs acquired and merged with, and it replaced the Curateurs name (TechCrunch 2016-08-19). No source explains why the name was chosen.
branding.domain_note: Used looklive.com. How it was obtained is not stated in sources found.

identity.visual_style: Photo-led celebrity imagery in a mobile shopping app
identity.voice_and_tone: Aspirational, 'dress like the stars' (Atlanta Magazine headline)

rebrands.why: Name taken from the acquired and merged company when the two products were combined (TechCrunch 2016-08-19)

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage in TechCrunch, PYMNTS, Business of Fashion and Atlanta Magazine. No evidence found of merch or fan communities.

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade press and a claimed 1 million monthly users, but no sourced evidence of a distinctive identity or brand driven growth.

pivots.to: Looklive, merged product focused on men's celebrity style, with a TV show shopping feature later
pivots.why: Curateurs reached 1 million users, acquired Looklive and merged the technologies (TechCrunch 2016-08-19)

outcome_analysis: The cause of Looklive's inactivity is not public. It launched through YC in 2016 with about 1 million claimed monthly users and a small seed, and later moved toward TV product placement data. A third party tracker estimates it ended around 2019 after about $2.0M burned, but no post-mortem or press report confirms the date or reason, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: Company site looklive.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch, so its status could not be confirmed. YC page lists founded 2015 while other profiles say 2011 or 2013. Funding sources conflict: TechCrunch says YC put in $140,000 with Judge Ventures and a seed under $1M; StartupIntros says a $140K seed led by Paul Judge; one Spanish government startup database lists a $120K seed and a roughly 2.0M euro Series A with no date, which rests on that single database and is recorded without an amount or date. Total raised is given as $2.35M by CB Insights and $2.4M by StartupIntros, so the rounds recorded are probably incomplete. End date of 2019 and $2.0M burned come from a single tracker and are unverified. Exit type is unknown, consistent with status Inactive but without a sourced shutdown. Audit fix: the 140K that Y Combinator invested is added (TechCrunch 2016-08-19). The Series A of about 2M euro (about 2.24M USD per FinSMEs) was announced in early September 2015 and led by Liberty Global Ventures and Volta Ventures per Unquote and FinSMEs; the Spanish government database (startups.one.gob.es) lists the same 2.0M euro without a date, and CB Insights dates it 2015-09, so the date is consistent across these but the figure in dollars rests on FinSMEs. The earlier undated empty Series A entry is replaced. Looklive appears to be Amsterdam based per FinSMEs.
